extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political theory; lawmakers and constitutional designers interested in representative government
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for how representative assemblies should be constituted and behave: their proper functions, limits, composition, and safeguards to secure liberty, skilled administration, and prevention of factional or majoritarian abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper office of representatives — watch and control, not govern
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of the function of governing, for which it is radically unfit, the proper office of a representative assembly is to watch and control the government; to throw the light of publicity on its acts; to compel a full exposition and justification of all of them which any one considers questionable; to censure them if found condemnable, and, if the men who compose the government abuse their trust, or fulfill it in a manner which conflicts with the deliberate sense of the nation, to expel them from office, and either expressly or virtually appoint their successors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly's power is ample in supervision: unlimited latitude of suggestion and criticism, applying or withholding national assent; the assembly should avoid assuming the actual function of governing and instead ensure ministers are honestly and intelligently chosen and held responsible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly as Committee of Grievances and Congress of Opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: Parliament has an office ... to be at once the nation's Committee of Grievances and its Congress of Opinions; an arena in which not only the general opinion of the nation, but that of every section of it ... can produce itself in full light and challenge discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a forum where every section and eminent individual can present views, be tested by adverse controversy, and where opinions overruled feel satisfied that they were heard, so that public opinion manifests itself and marshals support in presence of government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximize publicity and liberty of discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: By the utmost possible publicity and liberty of discussion, whereby not merely a few individuals in succession, but the whole public, are made, to a certain extent, participants in the government, and sharers in the instruction and mental exercise derived from it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicity enables parties/opinions to muster strength, cures illusions about numbers/power, and forces government to give way to manifest opinion without employing strength; discussion is the assembly's proper business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of functions — disjoin control from conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no means of combining these benefits except by separating the functions which guaranty the one from those which essentially require the other; by disjoining the office of control and criticism from the actual conduct of affairs, and devolving the former on the representatives of the Many, while securing for the latter, under strict responsibility to the nation, the acquired knowledge and practiced intelligence of a specially trained and experienced Few.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislation and administration are skilled labor needing special study; assemblies should suggest and supervise but leave day-to-day conduct to experienced officials; avoid assemblies attempting to 'do' what they should discuss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislation as skilled labor requiring specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: By such arrangements as these, legislation would assume its proper place as a work of skilled labor and special study and experience ... while the most important liberty of the nation ... would be fully preserved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use committees, specialized bodies or trained legislators/officials for actual drafting and technical detail; prevent desultory or ignorant amendment by whole assembly that produces ill-considered legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition must secure adequate mental qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The positive evils and dangers ... may be reduced to two heads: first, general ignorance and incapacity, or ... insufficient mental qualifications, in the controlling body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composition fails to ensure intelligence and knowledge, assemblies will encroach on executive province, be misled by false pretenses, enact bad laws, abrogate good ones, or tolerate proceedings that set law aside; constitution should aim to secure sufficient competency for superintendence and check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad representativeness — fair sample of all classes and intellects
rubrics_metrics.description: They are, when properly constituted, a fair sample of every grade of intellect among the people which is at all entitled to a voice in public affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representative bodies should indicate wants and be organs for popular demands; composition should enable diverse opinions and social sections to be heard and tested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diffuse exercise of public functions — wide participation
rubrics_metrics.description: The advantage in this respect lies with that which most widely diffuses the exercise of public functions; on the one hand, by excluding fewest from the suffrage; on the other, by opening to all classes of private citizens ... the widest participation in the details of judicial and administrative business; as by jury-trial, admission to municipal offices...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage broad suffrage and opportunities for citizens to participate in public roles to develop faculties and civic education; but balanced against other important objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against meddling and micro-management by assemblies
rubrics_metrics.description: It is, however, very likely, and is one of the dangers of a controlling assembly, that it may be lavish of powers, but afterwards interfere with their exercise; may give power by wholesale, and take it back in detail, by multiplied single acts of interference in the business of administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent assemblies from undermining executive authority through repeated interference; cultivate a general conviction of the injurious character of such meddling; reserve detailed administration to trained agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain constitutional instruments of last resort
rubrics_metrics.description: The alteration of bills by a committee of the whole House would cease, not by formal abolition, but by desuetude; the right not being abandoned, but laid up in the same armoury with the royal veto, the right of withholding the supplies, and other ancient instruments of political warfare, which no one desires to see used, but no one likes to part with, lest they should any time be found to be still needed in an extraordinary emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep certain extreme constitutional tools (veto, withholding supplies, reserved rights) in reserve as safeguards even if seldom used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent domination by sectional or 'sinister' interests
rubrics_metrics.description: We next proceed to the evils arising from the prevalence of modes of action in the representative body, dictated by sinister interests ... interests conflicting more or less with the general good of the community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design institutions and incentives to prevent ruling majorities or classes from pursuing policies serving narrow class interests at expense of general welfare (taxation bias, protectionism, anti-competition measures, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect minority rights against majority partiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Looking at democracy ... it is surely possible that the ruling power may be under the dominion of sectional or class interests ... Suppose the majority to be whites, the minority negroes ... is it likely that the majority would allow equal justice to the minority?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional protections and institutional constraints are necessary to prevent majorities from imposing unjust burdens or denying equal justice to minorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reliance on exalted disinterested motives — design for real human nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Governments must be made for human beings as they are ... It is only a disinterested regard for others ... which ever directs the minds ... of classes or bodies of men towards distant or unobvious interests; and it can not be maintained that any form of government would be rational which required as a condition that these exalted principles of action should be the guiding and master motives in the conduct of average human beings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional design should account for self-interest and corruption by power; do not expect average citizens or classes to always act from enlightened long-run interest; build safeguards and incentives accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine trained administration with popular freedom to avoid routine
rubrics_metrics.description: A bureaucracy always tends to become a pedantocracy ... The disease which afflicts bureaucratic governments ... is routine. ... An outside element of freedom is necessary to enable it to do effectually or permanently even its own business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a balance: allow bureaucracies to accumulate experience while exposing them to popular impulses and reforms so they do not ossify into mechanical routine; popular government enables original talent to prevail against obstructive routine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly as indicator of political trends for statesmen
rubrics_metrics.description: Where statesmen can assure themselves, far more certainly than by any other signs, what elements of opinion and power are growing and what declining, and are enabled to shape their measures with some regard not solely to present exigencies, but to tendencies in progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use parliamentary debate and visible contestation to read public opinion and trends so executives and ministers can shape policy with regard to long-term tendencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberation's legitimacy — hearing and testing opposing views
rubrics_metrics.description: A place where every interest and shade of opinion in the country can have its cause even passionately pleaded, in the face of the government and of all other interests and opinions, can compel them to listen, and either comply, or state clearly why they do not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberation must be open, adversarial where necessary, and allow minorities to be heard so that decisions rest on reasoned superiority of argument rather than mere will.
